claim_text: After TGF-beta withdrawal residency reverts, effector function does not

audit.primary_source_pmid: NO PMID — bioRxiv preprint. Europe PMC ID PPR1223917; DOI 10.64898/2026.02.11.705354; posted 2026-02-14, version 1. bioRxiv API queried 2026-08-14: "no articles found for published version" — NOT peer-reviewed as of audit date.
audit.primary_source_citation: Schmid K, Haimerl C, Stark J, Müller E, Merz L, Schenk R, Pistrenko K, Baumgarten J, Berberich K, Bauer U, Ehmer U, Laschinger M, Hüser N, Hartmann D, Böttcher JP, Schmid RM, Wiedemann GM. "Prolonged TGF-β locks NK cells in a dysfunctional state through persistent epigenetic remodeling of IRF, T-bet and EOMES binding sites." bioRxiv 2026.02.11.705354, posted 14 Feb 2026. Corresponding author Gabriela M. Wiedemann, TUM University Hospital, Munich. Archived: /home/user/aaa/refs/R3_PPR1223917.txt
audit.what_was_measured: In human peripheral-blood NK cells (healthy adult donors, TUM ethics 2025-584-S-NP), negatively enriched and cultured in vitro in IMDM+ with IL-15 (50 ng/mL) with or without TGF-β (10 ng/mL): cells were exposed to TGF-β for 7 days, then on day 7 either continued on TGF-β to day 17 or washed twice and rested in IL-15 alone for a further 10 days (withdrawal arm), with media exchanged for ALL arms on day 7. At day 17 the readouts were: (a) surface frequencies of CD103+, CD9+, CD49a+ NK cells and intracellular frequencies of GZMA+, GZMB+, IFN-γ+ NK cells by spectral flow cytometry (Cytek Aurora) in n=7 donors across 3 independent experiments; (b) MFI of GZMA and IFN-γ after 3–4 h restimulation with IL-12/IL-18, IL-2+IL-15, IFN-α, or plate-bound anti-NKp46/anti-NKG2D in n=5 donors; (c) bulk RNA-seq and bulk ATAC-seq on FACS-sorted live CD56+ cells at day 0, day 7 and day 17 in n=5 donors; (d) MitoTracker Green and TMRE at day 17; (e) Ki67. Separately, at 3 h / 24 h / 7 d only (NOT in the day-17 withdrawal arm), impedance-based killing of BxPC-3 PDAC targets at 1:1 E:T by xCELLigence in n=2 / 7 / 10 donors. A sort control separated CD103+ and CD103− NK cells at day 7 and recultured them separately. A separate observational arm profiled tumour-infiltrating NK cells from n=10 liver-tumour patients and blood NK cells from n=12 HCC patients, with ATAC-seq on n=3 HCC vs healthy donors — this arm is cross-sectional and applies no withdrawal.
audit.n_unit: healthy adult human blood donors (day-17 flow phenotype/function, 3 independent experiments); n=5 donors for RNA-seq/ATAC-seq and for restimulation MFI; n=3 donors for CUT&RUN; separate cross-sectional patient cohort n=10 tumour / n=12 blood / n=3 ATAC. NOT cells.
audit.controls: Parallel IL-15-only cultures at every timepoint; media exchange and washing performed for all arms on day 7 so handling is matched; RNA-seq/ATAC-seq analysis explicitly restricted to genes/regions attributable to TGF-β rather than IL-15 at day 7 (Fig. S4A); CD103+ and CD103− cells sorted at day 7 and recultured separately to exclude selective outgrowth of TR-negative cells as the cause of phenotype reversion (Fig. S3A-C); MitoTracker Green/TMRE at day 17 to exclude a metabolic explanation for sustained dysfunction (Fig. S3D); target cells cultured without NK cells as killing-assay control; donor-paired statistics (Wilcoxon signed-rank; paired t-test for Fig. 3E); RIN ≥ 8 gate on RNA; ENCODE blacklist/MAPQ/duplicate filtering on ATAC; yeast spike-in for CUT&RUN. MISSING: no second (longer) withdrawal timepoint beyond 10 days; no TGF-βR inhibitor arm at withdrawal to confirm signal is truly off; no cytotoxicity assay in the day-17 withdrawal arm; no division-tracking dye to match proliferative history between arms; no non-TGF-β dysfunction comparator.
audit.strongest_alternative_explanation: The dissociation may be a difference in RECOVERY TIME CONSTANT, not a difference in reversibility, confounded by differential proliferative history. (1) Only ONE withdrawal duration was tested (10 days), so "effector function does not revert" strictly means "had not yet reverted by day 10." Surface integrins CD103/CD9/CD49a are short-lived, directly SMAD-driven transcripts whose protein turns over fast, so they necessarily decay quickly once signal stops; granule content, IFN-γ competence and chromatin state re-accumulate on intrinsically slower timescales. Two molecule classes with different half-lives sampled at a single post-withdrawal timepoint will always look "dissociated." (2) TGF-β durably suppressed proliferation (reduced Ki67, Fig. S3E). Over the 10-day rest the IL-15-only control is dominated by cells that have divided repeatedly, while the withdrawal arm divides less — so the day-17 comparison confounds cell-intrinsic epigenetic imprinting with differential division history, which is precisely the mechanism by which chromatin marks and protein loads are diluted and reset. No CFSE/CTV division tracking was used to match this. (3) 17 days of continuous high-dose IL-15 in a dish is itself a powerful differentiating and epigenetically remodelling signal; the authors explicitly flag this as unresolved in their limitations. (4) The day-17 "effector function" readout is intracellular granzyme/IFN-γ protein plus transcript and accessibility — a marker proxy. The actual target-cell killing assay was run only at 3 h/24 h/7 d and never in the withdrawal arm, so persistence of the functional deficit itself is not demonstrated by a functional assay. NOTE: the naive alternative — that CD103+ cells were simply outcompeted by CD103− cells — IS excluded by the authors' sort-and-reculture control, which is a genuine strength.
audit.counter_evidence: FOUND, but indirect — no study located that runs a TGF-β withdrawal design in NK cells and reports the opposite result. (1) Rea A et al., Nat Immunol 2025, PMID 40119192 / PMC11957989 (archived /home/user/aaa/refs/R3_PMC11957989.txt): CRISPR SMAD4 knockout renders human NK cells resistant to TGF-β-mediated loss of NKG2D, granzyme B and cytotoxicity, while CD103/CD49a/ITGB1 induction is MAINTAINED and SMAD4-independent. This corroborates a dissociation between effector suppression and residency induction, but at the PATHWAY level and as PREVENTION (KO before exposure) — it does not test whether an established deficit reverses, so it neither confirms nor refutes R3's temporal claim. (2) Niehrs A et al., Nat Immunol 2025, PMID 41087727 / PMC12571907 (archived /home/user/aaa/refs/R3_PMC12571907.txt): human liver-transplant cohort shows CD56bright NK cell tissue residency is transient, with TR cells egressing via lymphatics and recirculating — in vivo human support for the "residency phenotype is a labile state" half, and evidentially far stronger than the dish, though it tests no TGF-β withdrawal and measures no effector persistence. (3) Cross-lineage partial counter-evidence, cited by the authors themselves (refs 64-68), that TGF-β-associated lymphocyte dysfunction is at least partly reversible by genetic or pharmacologic interference — e.g. Kwon M et al., Clin Cancer Res 2020, PMID 31941326 (PD-1 blockade plus TGF-β inhibitors reinvigorates myeloma bone-marrow CD8+ T cells) and Tran HC et al., Clin Cancer Res 2017, PMID 27756784 (galunisertib enhances NK-mediated anti-neuroblastoma activity). These involve ACTIVE pathway blockade rather than passive withdrawal, and mostly T cells, so they weaken the generality of "irreversible" without directly refuting the withdrawal experiment. No contradicting NK withdrawal study found.
audit.downstream_dependency: Directly constrains T1 ("cNK -> trNK, acquisition of a residency phenotype") and T4 ("NK -> ILC1 within tumours"). If CD49a/CD103/CD9 expression is a continuously signal-dependent STATE that decays within 10 days of TGF-β removal, then marker-defined "trNK" and "ILC1-like" endpoints in T1/T4/X3 cannot be read as stable lineage endpoints at all, and any marker-only ancestry inference in those rows is downgraded accordingly. Most concretely, R3's CD103+/CD103− sort-and-reculture control is the exact experimental design that T4's registered Occam alternative ("pre-existing convertible subset is selected") demands, so T4's alternative-explanation analysis can cite it. Load-bearing is MEDIUM rather than HIGH because the primary source is a single unrefereed in vitro preprint and because T1/T4 each carry independent in vivo evidence bases (parabiosis, adoptive transfer, transplant genotype) that do not depend on R3.
audit.audit_overturns_detail: CITATION UPHELD — unusually for this batch, the hint was accurate. Schmid K is first author and Wiedemann GM is corresponding/last author, ATAC-seq is central, and the paper reports exactly the asserted dissociation. TGF-β was genuinely withdrawn (washed twice on day 7, rested 10 days in IL-15), and chromatin and function were measured separately, as the hint required. CLASSIFICATION OVERTURNED — Claude called this "OBSERVATION." It is not any OBS_* class. The entire withdrawal experiment is in vitro: negatively-enriched human blood NK cells in a 96-well plate with recombinant IL-15 and recombinant TGF-β. There is no in vivo system, no adoptive transfer, no genetic fate mapping, and no tracking of any individual cell across the transition. Correct class is INF_INVITRO, with INF_MARKER (residency read out purely as CD103/CD9/CD49a surface staining and ITGAE/ZNF683/ITGA1/CD9 transcripts; day-17 "function" read out as intracellular granzyme/IFN-γ, not killing) and INF_KINETIC (durability inferred from a washout-plus-rest timecourse) also present. SECOND OVERTURN, unflagged by Claude: the source is an unrefereed bioRxiv preprint (v1, 14 Feb 2026), and the bioRxiv API confirms no published version exists as of 2026-08-14. A preregistered screen should not carry a preprint at OBSERVATION strength. THIRD: Claude's phrasing "effector function does not revert" overstates the assay — the day-17 withdrawal arm never received a cytotoxicity assay; persistence rests on intracellular protein, transcript and accessibility proxies. Per G2 no trajectory/pseudotime/velocity analysis is present, so INF_TRAJECTORY does not apply here.
audit.notes: EXPLICIT PER BATCH INSTRUCTION — R3 IS NOT A LINEAGE CLAIM. It does not assert "does A give rise to B." It is a two-part FUNCTIONAL/STATE-PERSISTENCE claim: (i) does a phenotype require continuous signal to be maintained, and (ii) does a functional deficit outlast removal of the signal that caused it. No ancestry, no progenitor-product relationship, and no cell is claimed to become a different cell. The one place it touches lineage is indirect and evidential rather than assertional: because it shows the residency marker set is signal-dependent and decays, it undercuts marker-based ancestry inferences made elsewhere in the screen (T1, T4, X3) — but that is R3 constraining other rows' lineage claims, not R3 being one itself. Note this is the mirror image of R1, which is likewise functional-not-lineage. SCOPE MISMATCH WORTH FLAGGING FOR A LATER PHASE: the claim as registered says "residency phenotype reverts." What was actually shown is that a TGF-β-INDUCED, IN VITRO residency-marker phenotype in blood-derived NK cells decays after TGF-β removal. That is not the same object as a bona fide tissue-resident NK cell established in vivo in a tissue niche, which is exposed to far more than TGF-β. Generalising from the former to the latter is an unlicensed jump. STRENGTHS, recorded so the downgrade is not read as dismissal: the CD103+/CD103− sort-and-reculture control genuinely excludes selective outgrowth; IL-15-only controls run in parallel throughout; the analysis is explicitly restricted to TGF-β-attributable features to subtract IL-15 effects; handling is matched across arms; metabolic confounding is tested and excluded; statistics are donor-paired. The authors' own limitations section is candid about the in vitro system and about unresolved long-term IL-15 effects. WEAKNESSES: unrefereed preprint; n=5 donors for all sequencing; a single 10-day withdrawal timepoint; no division tracking despite documented durable proliferation defect; no killing assay in the withdrawal arm. SEARCH NOTE per G3: counter-evidence status is FOUND (indirect) and is based on searches actually run and read, not on absence of results. The HCC patient arm is real in vivo human data but is cross-sectional and applies no withdrawal, so it cannot upgrade in_vivo for this claim; it is association only, and the authors concede other suppressive signals contribute.
audit.methods_quote: Methods, "Cultivation of NK cells": "In cases where TGF-β was withdrawn, cells were transferred to a low-bind tube, washed once with PBS, resuspended in fresh media, and transferred to a new well. All procedures were performed in U-bottom plates. For the 17-day setup, cells were neither handled nor supplemented between days 0-7 and 7-17." | Fig. 3A legend: "On day 7, media were exchanged for all conditions, and cells were maintained in IL-15 (control) or IL-15 + TGF-β. For the withdrawal condition, cells were washed twice on day 7 and cultured in IL-15 for an additional 10 days. Analyses were performed at days 0, 7, and 17." | Result: "Following TGF-β withdrawal for 10 days, TR markers largely returned to baseline, underscoring the requirement for continuous TGF-β signaling to maintain this phenotype (Fig 3B). ... In contrast to the reversibility of TR features, NK cell effector function demonstrated sustained impairment after TGF-β withdrawal. Reduced expression of granzyme A and B and IFN-γ was maintained even after 10 days of rest (Fig. 3C)." | Sort control: "CD103+ and CD103− NK cells were sorted after 7 days of TGF-β exposure and cultured separately... Both populations showed comparable loss of CD103 expression following TGF-β withdrawal (Fig. S3C)." | Authors' limitation: "Several limitations should be acknowledged, including the use of defined in vitro systems, which cannot fully capture the complexity of tissue environments in vivo... In addition, NK cells were maintained in IL-15 for prolonged culture periods, and long-term IL-15 exposure itself has been reported to induce transcriptional and epigenetic adaptations that may intersect with or modulate TGF-β-driven programs."

adv.challenge_reason:
INF_INVITRO UPHELD as strongest class, but on partly different grounds, and the prior row's methods reading contains three verifiable errors.

LINEAGE STATUS (batch instruction): R3 is NOT a lineage claim. It asserts nothing of the form "does A give rise to B." It is a two-part functional/state-persistence claim: (i) is a phenotype maintained only while its inducing signal is present, and (ii) does a functional deficit outlast the signal that caused it. No progenitor-product relationship is asserted or tested. Concur with prior auditor on this point only.

CLASSIFICATION, re-derived from Methods (refs/R3_PPR1223917.txt, "Cultivation of NK cells", "Bulk RNA sequencing", "Impedance-based killing assay"). Negatively enriched human PB NK cells, 6-12 wells of a 96-well U-bottom plate, IMDM+/10% FCS, rhIL-15 50 ng/mL +/- rhTGF-beta 10 ng/mL. No animal, no transfer, no fate map, no genetic perturbation of any kind (I grepped: no KO, no dominant-negative, no reporter). No OBS_* class applies. Per G2, no pseudotime/velocity/trajectory analysis exists, so INF_TRAJECTORY correctly absent. evidence_types_all [INF_INVITRO, INF_MARKER, INF_KINETIC] upheld.

G-RULE CHECK YOU ASKED FOR (population comparison credited as same-cell persistence) — the prior row did not articulate this and it bites at two levels. (a) WITHIN the withdrawal experiment: arms are donor-paired, so not different individuals, but they are different WELLS of cells. There is no barcoding, no division dye, no viability or cell-count reporting per arm, and no single-cell tracking. "The cells that were dysfunctional at day 7 are still dysfunctional at day 17" is a population-frequency inference across separate aliquots — INF_MARKER/INF_KINETIC, never an observation. (b) BETWEEN individuals: Fig. 7D-E compares ATAC-seq of sorted blood NK cells from n=3 HCC patients vs n=3 healthy donors, and Fig. 7C compares n=12 HCC vs healthy controls, to argue chronic TGF-beta imprinting operates in vivo. Cross-sectional, different people, no withdrawal — cannot evidence persistence. The prior auditor noted this arm was cross-sectional but MISSED that Fig. 7D's legend states the patients were selected "with reduced NK-cell functionality (n = 3)" — i.e. the epigenetics comparison is selected on the outcome it is used to explain, and a PCA separating 3 individuals from 3 individuals on the top 80,000 variable features is near-guaranteed regardless of mechanism.

THREE ERRORS IN THE PRIOR ROW'S METHODS READING. (1) Wash count is internally contradictory in the source and the prior row reproduced both without noticing: Methods says "transferred to a low-bind tube, washed ONCE with PBS"; Fig. 3A and Fig. 4 legends say "washed TWICE on day 7." The completeness of the central manipulation is not consistently specified. (2) The prior row's controls field asserts "media exchange and washing performed for all arms on day 7 so handling is matched." False. Fig. 3A says media were exchanged for all conditions, but the tube transfer + PBS wash + replating is described ONLY for the withdrawal arm. Handling is NOT matched; the withdrawal arm alone receives an extra mechanical/washing insult before the 10-day rest. (3) Neither the prior row nor the source acknowledges that Methods state "For the 17-day setup, cells were neither handled nor supplemented between days 0-7 and 7-17" — so both arms sat 10 days in unreplenished medium with a single day-7 IL-15 bolus. "No functional recovery" was therefore assayed under progressively depleted culture conditions, and the "continuous TGF-beta" arm is itself a decaying-signal arm.

CLAIM-SCOPE ASYMMETRY the prior row understated: the strongest class does not apply uniformly across the two halves. Half (i) (residency reverts) rests on surface staining — INF_MARKER. Half (ii) (effector does not revert) rests ONLY on intracellular GZMA/GZMB/IFN-gamma staining (Fig. 3B-C legends both say "Baseline frequencies", i.e. unstimulated content), restimulation MFI (Fig. 3E, n=5), transcript and accessibility. The xCELLigence killing assay was run at 3 h (n=2), 24 h (n=7) and 7 d (n=10) ONLY — never in any withdrawal arm, at day 17 or at the Fig. 2 6-day-rest arms. The abstract's "sustained suppression of cytotoxicity ... that persists even after signal withdrawal" is therefore not backed by any cytotoxicity measurement. This is exactly the G1 failure mode; the prior auditor flagged it as their "THIRD" overturn and was right to.
adv.new_counter_evidence:
STRONGEST NEW ITEM — THE PRIOR AUDITOR'S OWN CITATION POINTS THE OTHER WAY. Niehrs A et al., Nat Immunol 2025, PMID 41087727 / PMC12571907 (archived refs/R3_PMC12571907.txt) was credited by the prior row as "in vivo human support for the residency-phenotype-is-labile half." Reading the results, it is closer to a counter-observation. Two passages: (1) "NK cells from PB, EXCEPT donor-derived CD56bright NK cells, displayed lower expression of TR markers (CD49a, CXCR6, CD69 and CD103) compared to liver-derived NK cells" — i.e. after human liver transplantation, liver-origin CD56bright NK cells recovered from PERIPHERAL BLOOD, having left the TGF-beta-rich hepatic niche, still carry high CD49a/CXCR6/CD69/CD103. (2) "NK cells within the liver, liver-draining LNs and efferent lymph fluid displayed a consistent phenotype with Aiolos, Eomes, CXCR6 and CD54 expression, indicative of a conserved phenotype throughout the recirculation route" (thoracic-duct cannulation in humans, plus n=2 rhesus macaques). Niehrs shows the CELL's residency is transient (cells egress and are replaced); it does not show the residency PHENOTYPE decays once the cell leaves the niche — it shows the opposite. Those are different propositions and R3's Discussion conflates them (it cites Niehrs ref 70 and infers "TR as a potentially transient state"). Caveats, stated so this is not overread: lymphatic transit is hours-to-days, not 10 days; efferent lymph is not TGF-beta-free; and the explicitly "conserved" markers are Aiolos/Eomes/CXCR6/CD54 rather than CD103/CD49a. Niehrs also contains a genetic control R3 lacks — CRISPR RUNX3 KO in primary human NK cells abolishes TGF-beta-driven CD103 upregulation — showing residency-marker induction is not a bare readout of SMAD occupancy.

ALTERNATIVE EXPLANATION THE PRIOR AUDITOR MISSED, AND IT IS STRONGER THAN THEIRS. "Withdrawal" is never verified to be signal-off, and the paper's own data suggest it may not be. I grepped the full text: pSMAD2/SMAD3 phosphorylation is mentioned only as introductory background and is measured NOWHERE; there is no TGF-betaR inhibitor (SB431542/galunisertib) arm at withdrawal; there is no residual-TGF-beta ELISA. Meanwhile Fig. 4B reports that SMAD3 is among the PERSISTENTLY UPREGULATED genes after withdrawal. NK cells produce TGF-beta autocrinely and 10% FCS carries latent TGF-beta, so a low-level residual signal acting on an upregulated SMAD3 is entirely consistent with the data. Under that model the dissociation is a signal-THRESHOLD effect, not a reversibility difference: CD103/CD9/CD49a induction requires high sustained SMAD input and falls away, while effector repression is maintained by residual low-level signalling. This alternative is cleaner than the prior row's "different protein half-lives" story because it is positively supported by the source's own SMAD3 result, and it is not excluded by any control in the paper. The prior row's proliferation-dilution argument is also mis-signed: reduced Ki67 in the TGF-beta arm means the withdrawal arm divides LESS, which would preserve marks, so dilution cannot explain why residency marks are lost there.

CORROBORATING-BUT-NOT-DISPOSITIVE (prior auditor found these; I verified them and sharpen the reading). Rea A et al., Nat Immunol 2025, PMID 40119192 / PMC11957989, section header "SMAD4 uncouples TGFbeta inhibition from tissue residency in NK cells": CRISPR SMAD4 KO human NK cells resist TGF-beta-driven loss of effector function while TR integrin/chemokine-receptor induction is preserved SMAD4-independently. This is a peer-reviewed GENETIC dissociation of the two programs in human NK cells — evidentially stronger than R3's washout for the dissociation itself, but it tests prevention, not reversal, so it neither confirms nor refutes R3's temporal claim. Castriconi R et al., PNAS 2003, PMID 12646700 (TGF-beta1 represses NKp30/NKG2D) establishes the acute suppression baseline. Otegbeye F et al., PLoS One 2018, PMID 29342200 (TGF-beta inhibition preserves expanded NK function) is prevention, not rescue of an established deficit.

NO DIRECT REFUTATION EXISTS. I ran five distinct searches for an NK study performing TGF-beta washout and reporting functional recovery (queries listed in crossfield_searches_run) and read the returns; none exists. Per G3 this is FOUND-but-indirect, not absence of the phenomenon. R3 is currently the only source running this design in NK cells.

PEER-REVIEW STATUS RE-VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY: Europe PMC core query on DOI 10.64898/2026.02.11.705354 returns id PPR1223917, source PPR, pmid null, firstPublicationDate 2026-02-14; bioRxiv details API returns version 1, type "new results"; bioRxiv pubs API returns "no articles found for published version of". Unrefereed as of 2026-08-14. Citation itself UPHELD — Schmid K first author, Wiedemann GM corresponding, and the paper does report the asserted dissociation.
adv.crossfield_g4_findings:
The mechanism's home field is T cell exhaustion epigenetics, and it supplies both the design standard R3 fails and the specific artefact R3 is most likely showing.

1. DESIGN STANDARD R3 DOES NOT MEET. Philip M et al., Nature 2017, PMID 28514453 / PMC5693219 (archived refs/R3_G4_PMC5693219.txt) states the operational definition directly: "TST dysfunction is initially reversible but ultimately becomes irreversible, EVEN AFTER REMOVAL OF DYSFUNCTIONAL T CELLS FROM THE TUMOR MICROENVIRONMENT AND MULTIPLE ROUNDS OF CELL DIVISION." The field's test for signal-independent epigenetic fixity is (a) remove the cell from the inducing environment in vivo, and (b) demonstrate the state survives division. R3 does neither: no transfer, and no CFSE/CellTrace despite a documented durable Ki67 deficit. Philip also found the same duration threshold R3 reports (plastic state 1 at day 5-7, fixed state 2 from day 14), so R3's structural conclusion is field-consistent and unsurprising — which is a reason to treat it as low-novelty corroboration rather than as load-bearing new evidence.

2. THE SPECIFIC ARTEFACT PHILIP IDENTIFIED, WHICH R3 CANNOT EXCLUDE. Philip sorted CD38lo/CD101lo vs CD38hi/CD101hi cells out of a day-14 population that looked uniformly fixed in bulk; the lo/lo fraction fully regained IFN-gamma and TNF-alpha, the hi/hi fraction did not. A bulk frequency/MFI readout of an apparently "fixed" population can be a MIXTURE of recovered and non-recovered cells. R3's day-17 effector readout is exactly such a bulk readout. Note the asymmetry: R3 ran a sort-and-reculture control (CD103+/CD103-, Fig. S3A-C) for the RESIDENCY half, which is a genuine strength, but ran no heterogeneity control whatsoever for the EFFECTOR half — the half that carries the claim's weight.

3. "DOES NOT SPONTANEOUSLY REVERT" IS NOT "EPIGENETICALLY LOCKED." Ghoneim HE et al., Cell 2017, PMID 28648661: de novo DNMT3A-mediated methylation enforces exhaustion, and DNMT3A deletion or decitabine restores PD-1-blockade rejuvenation. Pauken KE et al., Science 2016, PMID 27789795 and Sen DR et al., Science 2016, PMID 27789799: exhaustion-specific enhancer landscapes are not remodelled by checkpoint blockade and reinvigoration is transient. Abdel-Hakeem MS et al., Nat Immunol 2021, PMID 34312545 (correction 34588688): epigenetic scars persist in vivo after chronic antigen is cleared. Net: durability after passive withdrawal is a real and expected phenomenon, but the causal word in R3's title — "locks" — requires an eraser/writer intervention that R3 never performs. R3 shows correlation between persistent DARs/H3K4me3 loss and persistent dysfunction, not that chromatin is what maintains it. (Searched for the TOX primaries, Khan et al. 2019; my queries returned no hit through lit.py and I did not retrieve them — NOT retrieved, though the TOX literature was not needed to reach this point.)

4. TRAINED IMMUNITY — WHERE THE MEMORY IS ACTUALLY STORED. Kleinnijenhuis J et al., PNAS 2012, PMID 22988082 attributed months-long BCG protection to epigenetic reprogramming of monocytes; because monocytes survive days in circulation, the field relocated the memory to the progenitor compartment: Kaufmann E et al., Cell 2018, PMID 29328912 (BCG educates HSCs); Cirovic B et al., Cell Host Microbe 2020, PMID 32544459 (human BCG trained immunity via the hematopoietic progenitor compartment); Immunity 2024, PMID 39153479 (BCG alters the epigenetic landscape of human bone-marrow progenitors). A closely analogous 2025 result, PMC12571872, shows hypoxia causes H3K4me3 loss in neutrophil PROGENITORS producing long-term functional impairment — the same mark R3 reports lost at effector promoters, but stored one compartment upstream. Bearing on R3: the dish experiment shows a mature human NK cell can hold a dysfunctional state for 10 days, which is a genuine but narrow result. It says nothing about where durable NK dysfunction resides in an HCC patient, and R3's Fig. 7 cross-sectional arm cannot distinguish cell-intrinsic imprinting in mature NK cells from continuous re-imposition on newly produced NK cells or from a reprogrammed progenitor compartment. The trained-immunity field learned this exact lesson the hard way.

5. ADJACENT NK PRECEDENT FOR DURABLE FUNCTIONAL IMPRINTS. Romee R et al., Sci Transl Med 2016, PMID 27655849 and Blood 2012, PMID 22983442: cytokine-induced memory-like NK cells retain an enhanced-function imprint for weeks. Durable functional imprinting in NK cells is established in the positive direction, which raises the prior on R3's phenomenon while doing nothing to validate its measurement.

adv.load_bearing_reason:
The prior row set MEDIUM and justified it by having R3 constrain T1 ("cNK -> trNK") and T4 ("NK -> ILC1 within tumours"). That justification is self-defeating: the same row's own notes concede that generalising from "a TGF-beta-induced residency-MARKER phenotype on blood-derived NK cells in a dish" to "a bona fide tissue-resident NK cell established in an in vivo niche" is "an unlicensed jump." The T1/T4 dependency IS that jump. You cannot flag an inference as unlicensed and then bank load-bearing weight on it.

Testing the dependency concretely: delete R3 from the screen and ask which downstream verdict changes.
- T1 does not move. Its evidence base is in vivo and independent: Sojka DK et al., eLife 2014, PMID 24714492 / PMC3975579 (parabiosis, archived T1_PMC3975579.txt); Cortez VS et al., Immunity 2016, PMC5114145; Cortez VS et al., Nat Immunol 2017, PMID 28759002 / PMC5712491.
- T4 does not move. Gao Y et al., Nat Immunol 2017, PMID 28759001 (archived T1_28759001.txt / T4_28759001.txt) carries it.
- The marker-lability premise R3 is invoked for is established better, peer-reviewed, and IN VIVO IN HUMANS by Niehrs A et al., PMID 41087727 — and, per my counter-evidence field, Niehrs points the opposite way on phenotype retention (liver-origin CD56bright NK cells retain CD49a/CXCR6/CD69/CD103 after entering peripheral blood; the TR phenotype is "conserved throughout the recirculation route"). So R3 is redundant where it agrees with stronger evidence and unlicensed where it would extend beyond it.

CONCRETE NAMED RESIDUAL DEPENDENCY, and it is methodological rather than evidential: T4's registered Occam alternative — "a pre-existing convertible subset is selected rather than converted" — is the alternative that R3's CD103+/CD103- sort-and-reculture control (Fig. S3A-C) is designed to exclude. T4's alternative-explanation analysis can therefore cite R3 as a design template. Citing a design is not depending on a result: if R3 vanished, T4 would still need to run or find that control, and R3 supplies no in vivo instance of it. That is a LOW dependency.

Three further reasons LOW is the correct level, not MEDIUM. (a) Source quality: an unrefereed bioRxiv v1 with no published version as of 2026-08-14 (verified via bioRxiv pubs API) should not carry MEDIUM weight on any downstream verdict in a preregistered screen when nothing downstream requires it. (b) Assay gap: the half of R3 that would matter most downstream — persistence of the FUNCTIONAL deficit — is never measured functionally after withdrawal; xCELLigence killing was run only at 3 h (n=2), 24 h (n=7) and 7 d (n=10), never in any washout arm. (c) Unexcluded confound: because pSMAD2/3 is never measured, no TGF-betaR inhibitor arm exists, and SMAD3 is itself persistently upregulated after withdrawal (Fig. 4B), the paper has not established that "withdrawal" equals "signal off" — so even the direction of R3's dissociation is not secured well enough to constrain another row.

If a later phase wants R3 upgraded, the two decisive additions are cheap and nameable: a pSMAD2/3 or TGF-betaR-inhibitor arm at day 17 to prove the signal is actually off, and a CD38/CD101-style sort of the day-17 population on the effector axis (Philip 2017, PMID 28514453) to show the bulk "fixed" phenotype is not a mixture of recovered and non-recovered cells.
adv.better_primary_source:
NO better primary source exists for R3 AS REGISTERED. I searched five distinct ways for any NK study running a TGF-beta withdrawal-and-rest design (queries listed in crossfield_searches_run) and read the returns; Schmid K, Haimerl C, ..., Wiedemann GM, "Prolonged TGF-beta locks NK cells in a dysfunctional state through persistent epigenetic remodeling of IRF, T-bet and EOMES binding sites," bioRxiv PPR1223917, DOI 10.64898/2026.02.11.705354, v1 posted 2026-02-14, NO PMID, no published version as of 2026-08-14, is the only source that performs the experiment. Citation UPHELD (archived /home/user/aaa/refs/R3_PPR1223917.txt). This is "searched and does not appear to exist," not "did not search."

But R3 is two claims welded together, and each half has a stronger peer-reviewed primary source that the screen should cite ALONGSIDE the preprint rather than resting on it:

(1) For the DISSOCIATION between the residency program and the effector program — Rea A et al., "Enhancing human NK cell antitumor function by knocking out SMAD4 to counteract TGFbeta and activin A suppression," Nat Immunol 2025, PMID 40119192 / PMC11957989 (archived refs/R3_PMC11957989.txt), section "SMAD4 uncouples TGFbeta inhibition from tissue residency in NK cells." Peer-reviewed, human, CRISPR genetic perturbation — an OBS_GENETIC-grade separation of the two programs versus R3's INF_INVITRO washout. It tests prevention, not reversal, so it does not cover R3's temporal axis, but for the dissociation itself it is strictly the better source.

(2) For the STABILITY OF THE RESIDENCY PHENOTYPE, which is the half the screen actually leans on downstream — Niehrs A et al., "Transient tissue residency and lymphatic egress define human CD56bright NK cell homeostasis," Nat Immunol 2025, PMID 41087727 / PMC12571907 (archived refs/R3_PMC12571907.txt). Peer-reviewed, in vivo, human liver-transplant cohort plus thoracic-duct efferent lymph plus rhesus macaque plus humanized mouse plus CRISPR RUNX3 KO. It is the correct primary source for whether marker-defined residency is a stable endpoint, and it should replace R3 in that role — noting it answers in the opposite direction on phenotype retention.

(3) For the MECHANISTIC PROPOSITION "prolonged signalling epigenetically fixes lymphocyte dysfunction," the field-standard primary source with the in vivo removal-plus-division control R3 lacks is Philip M et al., "Chromatin states define tumour-specific T cell dysfunction and reprogramming," Nature 2017, PMID 28514453 / PMC5693219 (archived refs/R3_G4_PMC5693219.txt).
